title: Reference-safety fixpoint must count both directions of supersession
context: Compaction's greatest-fixpoint algorithm protects records referenced by survivors. supersedeIn() sets old.superseded_by without requiring successor.supersedes — an asymmetric reference. The algorithm only checked `d.supersedes`, allowing removal of a rejected successor while a surviving record still pointed to it, creating a dangling pointer and permanently non-live topic. Touches invariant(s): con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_947c578b2c (Forward-migrate raw JSON to the current schema BEFORE Zod validation; never silently drop unmigratable records); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Extended the fixpoint reference-collection phase to protect both `d.supersedes` and `d.superseded_by` edges. Any surviving decision whose outgoing pointer targets a removal candidate is rescued, ensuring no orphaned pointers and preserving topic liveness through compaction.
consequences: Eliminates data-structure corruption (dangling pointers in supersession chains)
Survivors maintain liveness invariant: each decision remains reachable for its topic after compaction
Fixpoint iteration now terminates with complete reference closure, not partial
alternatives_rejected: Make supersedeIn() bidirectional (set both directions) — loses the intentional asymmetry; requires API redesign elsewhere
Disable successor removal entirely — prevents legitimate pruning of rejected decisions
Post-compaction validation with repair — treats symptom; already-deployed corrupted graphs remain broken
